# User Story: [SAP] Automate PDF Download/Save from SAP GUI

Source: `SAP Ingenious Issues 2026.xlsx` — sheet `SAP Requests` (Item #4), sheet `US`.

## User Story

As an INGenious engineer, I want to automate the saving and downloading of PDF documents
generated from SAP, so that document validation and downstream automation steps can be performed
without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria (ATDD)

### Scenario 1: Save PDF generated by SAP

**Given** a SAP transaction generates a PDF document

**When** the Save PDF action is executed

**Then** the PDF is saved successfully to the configured location

### Scenario 2: Handle desktop save dialog

**Given** SAP opens a Windows save dialog

**When** automation reaches the dialog

**Then** the framework can interact with the dialog and complete the save process

### Scenario 3: Validate downloaded file

**Given** the PDF save operation completes

**When** execution continues

**Then** the framework can verify that the file exists in the target location

### Scenario 4: Use downloaded file in subsequent steps

**Given** a PDF has been saved

**When** later steps reference the file

**Then** the file is available for validation or further processing

### Scenario 5: Documentation is updated

**Given** PDF download functionality is implemented

**When** documentation is updated

**Then** examples and usage guidance are available in ingenious-doc

## Related SAP Request Items

### Item #4

**Description:** Not able to determine steps for saving PDF document on the downloads.

**Additional Context:** SAP process navigates outside SAP to the Windows desktop download/save
dialog for saving the generated PDF file.

**Comment:** POC - Saving PDF file from SAP GUI.

## Context

Many SAP transactions generate PDF outputs that must be saved locally for validation, auditing,
or downstream processing. Users currently cannot automate the complete save process from SAP
through the download dialog.

## Goal

Provide automation support for downloading and saving PDF files generated by SAP transactions.

## Value

- Eliminates manual download activities.
- Enables document validation automation.
- Supports end-to-end business process testing.
- Improves automation coverage for SAP reporting transactions.

## Scope

Affected Components:

- SAP Automation Framework
- Desktop Interaction Engine
- File Download Utilities
- Workflow Actions
- Execution Runtime

## Current State (gap analysis)

**The one existing "download" action is 100% browser-specific and structurally cannot reach a
native Windows dialog.** `DownloadFiles.DownloadandSaveAs()`
(`Engine/src/main/java/com/ing/engine/commands/browser/DownloadFiles.java`) works by intercepting
Playwright's own `Page.waitForDownload(...)` event and calling `Download.saveAs(...)` - it never
touches the OS file system dialog at all, because Playwright suppresses the native Save dialog
and hands the browser download straight to the automation code as a `Download` object. SAP GUI
has no equivalent interception point: per Item #4's own description, the PDF save flow **leaves
the SAP GUI Scripting object model entirely** and opens a genuine Windows Common Item Dialog
(the same native `#32770`-class Save As dialog every Windows app uses) - not a `GuiComponent`,
not a browser page element, so neither JACOB (`SapGuiSession`/`SAPElement`) nor Playwright
(`Page`/`Locator`) can address it. This is a different, unrelated class of problem from every
other gap this session has addressed - those were all about talking to elements *inside* the SAP
GUI Scripting tree; this one is about a window *outside* it.

**No SAP action or driver currently touches anything outside the JACOB/SAP GUI object tree.**
Every action in `SAPActions.java` operates on `SAPElement`/`SAPsession` (JACOB `Dispatch`
objects). `SapDriverCreation` (added this session for screenshots) is the first piece of SAP
automation code in this codebase to reach *outside* JACOB into OS-level APIs - via
`java.awt.Robot` for pixel capture. That's a directly relevant precedent: `Robot` also supports
`keyPress`/`keyRelease` for simulating OS-level keyboard input, not just screen capture, and it's
already a proven, dependency-free technique in this codebase for stepping outside the SAP GUI
Scripting object model.

**A stronger existing precedent for native-window control already exists, in the IDE module.**
`IDE/src/main/java/com/ing/ide/main/mainui/playwrightrecording/InspectorWindowController.java`
shells out to `powershell.exe` with an inline C# snippet -
`[DllImport("user32.dll")] ... ShowWindowAsync(IntPtr hWnd, int nCmdShow)` via PowerShell's
`Add-Type` - to manipulate a window by handle from Java without any native/JNI dependency. This
is a real, already-shipped technique in this codebase for doing exactly the class of thing a Save
dialog needs (find a window, bring it to front, drive it) that goes beyond what pure `Robot`
keystrokes can verify.

**AutoIt is already "in the ecosystem" here, but only as a design-time script converter, not a
runtime engine.** `IDE/src/main/java/com/ing/ide/main/sapscript/parser/SapParserLangAutoIt.java`
and the commented-out "AutoIt (.au3)" import menu item in `AppMenuBar.java`/`AppActionListener.java`
exist to **parse** existing recorded AutoIt scripts into INGenious steps at design time - AutoIt
itself is never installed or executed by INGenious at runtime. So while the team has clearly
already recognized AutoIt as *a* tool for native-dialog automation (it's a well-known SAP GUI
Scripting companion for exactly this native-dialog problem), that recognition hasn't produced a
runtime capability - it's a migration path for legacy scripts, not a solution to Item #4.

**No file-existence/wait-for-file action exists anywhere in the framework today**, addressing
Scenario 3/4's gap directly. Every `Files.exists(...)`/`new File(...).exists()` call in the
codebase (~80 occurrences) is internal framework plumbing (project/settings/data-sheet loading,
multipart file-upload attachment in `Webservice.java`) - none of it is exposed as a testable
`@Action`. This gap isn't SAP-specific either: the browser's own `DownloadFiles.DownloadandSaveAs()`
has the exact same unaddressed need to assert/wait-for the downloaded file and reference its path
in later steps.

## Proposed Actions

1. **`sapSaveDialogConfirm`** (new SAP action, `Robot`-based, no new dependency) - the minimal POC:
   assumes the native Save dialog's filename field already has focus (the normal Windows default
   when such a dialog opens), select-all (`Ctrl+A`) + type the full destination path via
   `Robot.keyPress`/`keyRelease`, then press Enter. Cheapest to build (reuses exactly the `Robot`
   technique `SapDriverCreation` already established this session), but fragile: there is no way
   to confirm the dialog actually exists or is ready before typing - if the dialog is slow to
   appear, the keystrokes go wherever focus currently is instead. Needs a configurable delay
   before sending keys as a stopgap.

2. **`sapSaveDialogConfirm` (PowerShell/Win32 variant, alternative implementation)** - mirrors
   `InspectorWindowController`'s existing `Add-Type`/`DllImport("user32.dll")` pattern: shell out
   to `powershell.exe` to find the Save dialog by window class (`#32770`) and title, wait/poll for
   it to exist (with a timeout that fails the action clearly if it never appears, unlike the blind
   `Robot` approach), then set the filename field's text and invoke the Save button directly by
   window handle instead of trusting keyboard focus. More reliable and independently verifiable,
   at the cost of spawning a process per save and being materially more code than option 1.

3. **`assertFileExists` / `waitForFileExists`** (new `GeneralOperations` actions, not SAP-specific)
   - addresses Scenario 3/4 directly, and is deliberately general-purpose since the browser's
     `DownloadFiles.DownloadandSaveAs()` has the identical gap today. `waitForFileExists` polls
     with a timeout (a save can take a moment after the dialog is confirmed); `assertFileExists`
     is the immediate check. The resolved file path can then be stored via the existing
     `addVar`/`putUserDefinedData` plumbing (no new storage mechanism), so later steps reference
     it exactly like any other captured value from this session's SAP actions.

## Open Questions

- **Blind `Robot` keystrokes (option 1) vs PowerShell/Win32 window control (option 2) for the
  POC?** Option 1 is simpler and dependency-free but unverifiable (can't confirm the dialog
  exists before typing); option 2 is more reliable and matches an existing precedent in this
  codebase, but costs a process spawn per save and more implementation surface. Not yet decided
  which to build first for the POC - leaning option 2 given `InspectorWindowController` already
  proves the pattern works in this codebase, but option 1 may be enough for a first POC.
- **Dialog readiness detection** - if option 1 is chosen, how long to wait before assuming the
  dialog is ready (fixed delay vs polling window title/class via the same `Robot`/AWT APIs used
  for screenshots)? A fixed delay is simplest but inherently flaky under system load.
- **Overwrite-confirmation dialog** - if a file with the target name already exists at the
  destination, Windows shows a second "Confirm Save As" prompt before the first dialog closes.
  Does `sapSaveDialogConfirm` need to detect and dismiss that secondary dialog too, or is
  overwrite handling out of scope for this POC (caller responsible for unique filenames)?
- **Scope of `assertFileExists`/`waitForFileExists`** - confirmed general-purpose
  (`GeneralOperations`), not SAP-only, since the browser download gap is identical - no
  disagreement expected here, just needs to be built with both use cases in mind rather than
  assuming a SAP-only caller.
